title: Practice 2: Perfective or imperfective? The prefixed verbs in use

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: The dog ran away from us.
exercises.why: **убежала** is the past tense (feminine) of **убежать** (to run away, to make off, to flee; to escape) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **убегать**. past: он убежа́л · она убежа́ла · оно убежа́ло · они убежа́ли. — Wiktionary, «убежать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **убегала** is imperfective (**убегать**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **приплыли** is the past tense (plural) of **приплыть** (to swim up, to come swimming, to sail up) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приплывать**. past: он приплы́л · она приплыла́ · оно приплы́ло · они приплы́ли. — Wiktionary, «приплыть» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **приплывали** is imperfective (**приплывать**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: He ushered me to the hall.
exercises.why: **проводил** is the past tense (masculine) of **проводить** (to spend (time), to pass; (electricity) to conduct) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **провести**. past: он проводи́л · она проводи́ла · оно проводи́ло · они проводи́ли. — Wiktionary, «проводить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**про-** — Movement across, through, or past something Example: Мы проехали через город. — We drove through the city. Мы прошли мимо станции метро. — We passed the metro station. Prepositional phrases: сквозь / через / в + acc.; мимо + gen.; without preposition.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Compare: «Как вы проводите время?» (How do you spend your time?) — DLI, Lesson 79. «Я хорошо провёл время.» (I had a good time.) — DLI, Lesson 79.  The other choice: **провёл** is perfective (**провести**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **залезла** is the past tense (feminine) of **залезть** (to climb up (finished action); (also figurative) to get into, to scramble) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **залезать**. past: он зале́з · она зале́зла · оно зале́зло · они зале́зли. — Wiktionary, «залезть» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**за-** — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way Example: Старушка зашла за угол и исчезла. — The old woman walked behind the corner and disappeared. Prepositional phrases: в / на / за + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **залезала** is imperfective (**залезать**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: John came running into the room.
exercises.why: **вбежал** is the past tense (masculine) of **вбежать** (to come running in, to come rushing in, to run (into)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **вбегать**. past: он вбежа́л · она вбежа́ла · оно вбежа́ло · они вбежа́ли. — Wiktionary, «вбежать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**в-, во-** — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering. Antonym: вы- Example: Трамвай остановился, и девушка вошла. — The tram stopped and the girl entered. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **вбегал** is imperfective (**вбегать**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **пришёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **прийти** (to come (to), to arrive (at)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приходить**. past: он пришёл · она пришла́ · оно пришло́ · они пришли́. — Wiktionary, «прийти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Note. — The verbs приходить and приезжать usually refer to the habitual or repeated actions: Он приходит (приезжает) сюда каждый день. — He comes here every day. These verbs, as the other verbs of motion, may be used to express a single action in the future: Он приходит на работу завтра утром. — He is coming to work tomorrow morning. Она приезжает из Москвы сегодня вечером. — She is coming (arriving) from Moscow this evening. When the action is in progress in the present such expressions as "He is coming" or "He is on the way here" are expressed in Russian in the following way: Кто это идёт (едет) сюда?» — DLI, Lesson 24.  Compare: «Приходите сюда завтра!» (Come here tomorrow!) — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choice: **приходил** is imperfective (**приходить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **отошёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **отойти** (to go away, to go aside, to move away, to move aside; (military) to withdraw, to fall back) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **отходить**. past: он отошёл · она отошла́ · оно отошло́ · они отошли́. — Wiktionary, «отойти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**от-, ото-** — Withdrawal a short distance away. Antonym: под- Example: Мальчик отошёл от незнакомца, который предложил ему конфеты. — The boy stepped back from the stranger who had offered him candy. Prepositional phrases: от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Compare: «Я съезжу на вокзал и узнаю, когда отходит поезд.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  The other choice: **отходил** is imperfective (**отходить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **отвозил** is the past tense (masculine) of **отвозить** (to take away (by vehicle), to drive away, to take (someone or something by vehicle)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **отвезти**. past: он отвози́л · она отвози́ла · оно отвози́ло · они отвози́ли. — Wiktionary, «отвозить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**от-, ото-** — Withdrawal a short distance away. The other choice: **увозили** is imperfective (**увозить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: A sigh fell from her lips.
exercises.why: **слетел** is the past tense (masculine) of **слететь** (to fly down (from), to fly away (from); (colloquial) to fall down (from), to fall (off)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **слетать**. past: он слете́л · она слете́ла · оно слете́ло · они слете́ли. — Wiktionary, «слететь» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**с-, со-** — Movement downwards. Antonym: вз- Example: После представления актёр сошёл со сцены. — After the performance, the actor got off the stage. Prepositional phrases: с + gen.; на + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **слетал** is imperfective (**слетать**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

Prepositional phrases: в / на / за + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **заносило** is imperfective (**заносить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: The small dog crossed the road.
exercises.why: **перешла** is the past tense (feminine) of **перейти** (to cross, to get over, to get across; to pass on (to), to proceed (to), to turn (to)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **переходить**. past: он перешёл · она перешла́ · оно перешло́ · они перешли́. — Wiktionary, «перейти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**пере-** — Movement across, from one point to another; through Example: Утки переплыли реку. — The ducks swam across the river. Prepositional phrases: через + acc.; without preposition + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).
